'''Daniel Andrew Janies''' is an American scientist who has made significant contributions in the field of evolutionary biology and on the development of tools for the study of evolution and the spread of pathogens.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Janies|first1=Daniel A.|last2=Pomeroy|first2=Laura W.|last3=Krueger|first3=Chris|last4=Zhang|first4=Yuqi|last5=Senturk|first5=Izzet F.|last6=Kaya|first6=Kamer|last7=Çatalyürek|first7=Ümit V.|date=2015-12-01|title=Phylogenetic visualization of the spread of H7 influenza A viruses|journal=Cladistics|language=en|volume=31|issue=6|pages=679–691|doi=10.1111/cla.12107|pmid=34753271|s2cid=85577454|issn=1096-0031|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osc.edu/press/researchers_publish_article_on_tracking_infectious_disease|title=Researchers publish article on tracking infectious disease {{!}} Ohio Supercomputer Center|website=www.OSC.edu|date=31 May 2012|language=en|access-date=July 9, 2017}}</ref> He is involved with research for the [[United States Department of Defense]] and has advised multiple instances of the government on methods for disease surveillance.

== Education and career ==
Daniel Janies graduated in 1988 from the [[University of Michigan]], where he received his Bachelor of Sciences in Biology. He then pursued a Ph.D. in Zoology at the [[University of Florida]], which he completed in 1995. From 1996 until 2002 he was involved at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] in New York City, initially as a postdoctoral fellow (until 1999) and then as principal investigator (until 2002).{{citation needed|date=July 2017}}

His career as a faculty member started at the College of Medicine at the [[Ohio State University]] from 2003 until 2012, and lately he transitioned to the Department of Bioinformatics and Genomics of the [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte]] where he received the title of The Carol Grotnes Belk Distinguished Professor of Bioinformatics and Genomics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bioinformatics.uncc.edu/directory/janies-daniel|title=Janies, Daniel {{!}} Department of Bioinformatics and Genomics {{!}} UNC Charlotte|website=bioinformatics.uncc.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/danieljanies|title=LinkedIn|last=Janies|first=Daniel|website=LinkedIn|access-date=July 9, 2017}}</ref>

== Congressional testimony ==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=July 2017}}
Daniel Janies gave a testimony as part of the Testimony of the American Museum of Natural History on the Hearings of The United States House of Representatives Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense in 2010. He also gave a statement on Evaluation Roles, Preparedness for and Surveillance of Pandemic Influenza to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the United States Senate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov/congressional-report/111th-congress/senate-report/360/1|title=S. Rept. 111-360 - ACTIVITIES OF THE COMMITTEE ON HOMELAND SECURITY AND GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS|website=www.Congress.gov|access-date=January 17, 2018}}</ref>
